name: Maryland
summary: Statutes and the Constitution: mgaleg.maryland.gov StatuteText pages are constructible from (article code, section) and give one section per page (script route verified; WebFetch needs per-URL approval for built URLs); per-article PDFs under /{YYYY}RS/Statute_Web/ are the bulk/corpus route; Justia (2025) is the WebFetch-readable tier-2. Maryland Rules are online only on Westlaw's government site, which refuses automated access; only amendment Rules Orders are free on mdcourts.gov, and no tier-2 host carries the Rules. COMAR moved to regs.maryland.gov (Open Law Library; constructible per regulation, bulk XML on GitHub; unofficial text); the Maryland Register's last 15 issues are free as HTML on dsd.maryland.gov. Case law: mdcourts.gov serves reported Supreme Court / Appellate Court opinions from 1995 through a plain-GET index (official and UELMA-authenticated since July 1, 2018, but slip pagination only) and unreported Appellate Court opinions from May 2015 by monthly list; certiorari grants/denials are monthly HTML lists searchable only by party name.

citation_map.notes: Court renaming: effective Dec. 14, 2022 the Court of Appeals of Maryland became the Supreme Court of Maryland and the Court of Special Appeals became the Appellate Court of Maryland (name change only; mdcourts.gov opinions page). Pre-2022 'Court of Appeals' = the HIGH court (reporter Md.), not an intermediate court; pre-2022 'Ct. Spec. App.' = today's Appellate Court (reporter Md. App.). mdcourts.gov URLs still use 'coa' and 'cosa'. Statutes: the Code is cited by ARTICLE name, never by title number: Bluebook 'Md. Code Ann., Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-101'; Maryland courts write 'Md. Code (1974, 2020 Repl. Vol.), § 5-101 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article' or define a short form ('CJP § 5-101', 'CP § 8-301.1'). law_aliases maps every full name, Bluebook abbreviation and practitioner short form to the mgaleg article code (gcj, gcr, grp ...). Two- and three-letter short forms (CP, CR, CJ, RP, FL, ET, SG, IN, ED, CA, LE ...) are matched case-sensitively and only immediately before '§'; route them here only with Maryland context, because 'CP § ' or 'CA § ' also occur elsewhere (e.g. California). Bare article names shared with other states ('Real Property', 'Criminal Law', 'Insurance', 'Education', 'Family Law') must not route here without 'Md.'/'Maryland'/'Article' context. Section numbers are title-subtitle-section with hyphens, and some subtitles carry a letter (CJP § 3-2A-04, HG § 19-3B-01); the regex accepts a three-part number only when the middle part has a letter, so a range '§§ 10-1601–10-1611' yields 10-1601 (first section), never a fused number. Pages print sections with an EN DASH (§5–101); fetch_doc.py verify normalises dashes. Constitution: 'Md. Const. art. IV, § 14' → mgaleg article c4, section 14; Declaration of Rights 'Md. Const. Decl. of Rts. art. 24' / 'Article 24 of the Maryland Declaration of Rights' → c0, section 24; lettered articles XI-A … XI-I → c11A … c11I. Maryland Rules: 'Md. Rule 2-322(b)' (title-chapter+rule); Attorneys' Rules of Professional Conduct are Title 19 ('Md. Rule 19-301.7' = MARPC 1.7: Rule 1.x → 19-301.x, 2.x → 19-302.x … 8.x → 19-308.x). Bare 'Rule 2-322' must not route here without Maryland context. COMAR 'TT.SS.CC.RR' (title may carry a letter: 13A, 10A); Register Bluebook 'NN Md. Reg. PPP' and COMAR history form 'V:I Md. R. PPP' (volume:issue). Unreported Appellate Court opinions are cited by docket 'No. NNNN, Sept. Term, YYYY (Md. App. date)'; Md. Rule 1-104 lets those issued on or after July 1, 2023 be cited for persuasive value only. Maryland has no public-domain citation. Docket numbers: Supreme Court 'No. N, September Term, YYYY' (term year = the court's term, not the decision year; opinion PDFs sit under the FILING year); Appellate Court 'No. NNNN, September Term, YYYY' (4-digit, zero-padded in URLs). The docket form is shared by both courts and by other bodies using 'Term' dockets: route on it only with Maryland context. Westlaw cites route here only with a '(Md.' parenthetical. Examples marked with round reporter numbers (e.g. '300 A.3d 1 (Md. 2023)', '475 Md. 1') are form examples for the regex, not real citations. CourtListener ids 'md' and 'mdctspecapp' are from memory and unverified.

sources.title: Maryland General Assembly — Statutes Text (Annotated Code of Maryland, by article)
sources.official_status_evidence: No disclaimer or authentication statement on the StatuteText page. Md. Code Ann., State Gov't § 10-1601(d)(3) names DLS as official publisher of the Code, but UELMA (§ 10-1602) applies only to material designated official under § 10-1603; no designation shown on the page.
sources.coverage: All 36 articles of the Annotated Code plus the Constitution (articles c0 = Declaration of Rights, c1-c20). One section per page.

access.pattern_rules: article = three-letter code from the Statutes page table (gcj Courts and Judicial Proceedings, gcr Criminal Law, gcp Criminal Procedure, grp Real Property, ghg Health - General, gsg State Government, gtg Tax - General ... — see citation_map.law_aliases). section = the section number exactly as cited with ASCII hyphens (5-101, 3-2A-04, 8-301.1, 10-1601); no padding. enactments=false shows the law in effect January 1 of this year; enactments=true includes the last session's enactments (in effect October 1) — use true after October 1. A non-existent section returns HTTP 200 with the page heading 'File Not Found', not a 404.

automation.notes: WebFetch of the built StatuteText URL returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (permission prompt unanswered); no search result surfaced a StatuteText URL, so WebFetch could not be tested on this route. The script route reads the full section (5-101: 8.4K chars of page, section text after the 'Statutes Text' heading).

currency.where: Statutes index page radio buttons only; no currency line on section pages
currency.observed: Yes (Show statutes in effect as of October 1st of this year)

hazards: section headings use an en dash (§5–101): exact-match tools must normalise dashes
missing section returns 200 'File Not Found' rather than 404
enactments=false vs true changes which version is shown (Jan. 1 vs Oct. 1)
WebFetch needs per-URL approval for built URLs (gated)
page chrome (menus, open-data dialog) surrounds the section text

sources.title: Maryland General Assembly — Statute_Web PDFs (per section and per article)
sources.official_status_evidence: No authentication statement in the PDFs; see md-code-mgaleg.
sources.coverage: Per-section PDFs and whole-article PDFs for every article and constitution article, in a folder per session year (2019RS … 2027RS observed). The 2027RS folder (files dated Aug.–Sept. 2026) reflects the law after the 2026 session; older folders are frozen snapshots (2024RS c0.pdf still shows Declaration of Rights Art. 48 'NOT IN EFFECT ** SUBJECT TO REFERENDUM NOVEMBER 2024').

access.pattern_rules: article = mgaleg code (gcj, grp, c0, c4 ...); section with ASCII hyphens (5-101). YYYY = the NEXT regular session year relative to the text you want: after the 2026 session use 2027RS (Last-Modified Sept. 2026); 2026RS holds text as of Dec. 2025. Check Last-Modified via fetch_doc.py info and prefer the newest folder that exists.
